title: Christ speaks inwardly (III.1)
hook: blessed is the soul that hears the Lord speaking within
tomorrow: what's the one thing that makes heavy things feel light?

segments.voice: This week's six came in pairs and turns, from a calm voice to a heavy cross: peace first, two wings, above all, a familiar friend, to the cup. Then the royal way of the cross, and yesterday's line: carry it, it carries you.
screen: `CARRY IT, IT CARRIES YOU.` → `A WEEK IN BOOK TWO.`

segments.voice: Buzz: a group chat. Buzz: a sale. Buzz: someone liked a photo from last spring. The loudest things in a day aren't always the ones that matter. The voice that matters, the one that says slow down, or call her back, or you are loved, hardly ever buzzes. Book three of the Imitation opens on that problem. Until now one voice has been giving counsel. From here on, the book becomes mostly a conversation: the disciple speaks, and Christ answers.
screen: `BUZZ, BUZZ, BUZZ.` → `THE VOICE THAT DOESN'T BUZZ.` → `BOOK THREE: A CONVERSATION.`

segments.voice: It begins with a psalm. In the Douay-Rheims: "I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me." Then the blessings. Blessed is the soul, the chapter says, that hears the Lord speaking within, in the Latin, in se loquentem, and takes from his mouth a word of comfort. Blessed are the ears that catch God's quiet whisper and pay no attention to the whispering of the world. Blessed are the ears that listen, not to the voice sounding outside, but to the truth teaching within. So the disciple tells his own soul: shut the doors of your senses for a while, so you can hear what the Lord your God says in you. And when Christ speaks, his first words are simple: I am your salvation, your peace, your life; stay with me and you'll find peace. Nothing here promises a voice out loud. It's a listening, under the buzz. Less noise, more ear: that's the whole practice. Now look back at the week, because it led here. Peace first steadied the listener. Two wings simplified the aim. Above all set the order. A familiar friend made the talk possible. The cup and the royal way kept the friendship through hard days. Book two taught the inner life. Book three lets the inner voice speak.
screen: `I WILL HEAR WHAT THE LORD WILL SPEAK.` · `BLESSED ARE THE EARS.` · `SHUT THE DOORS OF THE SENSES.` · `I AM YOUR PEACE.` · then, large: `THE LORD SPEAKING WITHIN.`

segments.voice: Turn your phone face down and listen to the room until you can name one sound under the others: a fan, traffic, your own breath. Stay with it, then listen underneath it, for nothing in particular, the way you'd lean toward a friend across a noisy table. If you pray, begin with the psalm: I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me.
Christ speaks inwardly. The first chapter of book three: blessed is the soul that hears the Lord speaking within, beneath the world's noise.
Hold onto this: speaking within, quieter than every buzz and worth the wait. Another week, folded and put away.
